title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 22 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Chronicles chapter 22 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 22 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Chronicles Chapter 22.

questions.question: In 2 Chronicles 22, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ahaziah king
Ahaziah was forty and two years old when he began to reign
Ahaziah walked in the ways of the house of Ahab
Ahaziah's mother was his counsellor to do wickedly
questions.correctAnswer: The inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ahaziah king
questions.explanation: The first verse, 2 Chronicles 22:1, states that the inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ahaziah king.

questions.question: Who did the inhabitants of Jerusalem make king in place of Jehoram?
questions.correctAnswer: Ahaziah his youngest son
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 22:1 states that the inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ahaziah his youngest son king in his stead.

questions.question: Who had slain all the eldest sons, allowing Ahaziah to become king?
options: The band of men that came with the Arabians
questions.correctAnswer: The band of men that came with the Arabians
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 22:1 mentions that the band of men that came with the Arabians to the camp had slain all the eldest sons.

questions.question: How old was Ahaziah when he began to reign?
questions.correctAnswer: Forty and two years old
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 22:2 states that Ahaziah was forty and two years old when he began to reign.

questions.question: How long did Ahaziah reign in Jerusalem?
questions.correctAnswer: One year
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 22:2 states Ahaziah reigned one year in Jerusalem.

questions.question: What was the name of Ahaziah's mother?
questions.correctAnswer: Athaliah
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 22:2 says his mother's name was Athaliah, the daughter of Omri.

questions.question: Athaliah was the daughter of whom?
questions.correctAnswer: Omri
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 22:2 states Athaliah was the daughter of Omri.

questions.question: In what ways did Ahaziah walk?
options: In the ways of the house of Ahab
In the ways of the prophets
questions.correctAnswer: In the ways of the house of Ahab
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 22:3 states Ahaziah walked in the ways of the house of Ahab.

questions.question: Who was Ahaziah's counsellor to do wickedly?
questions.correctAnswer: His mother
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 22:3 states his mother was his counsellor to do wickedly.

questions.question: Why did Ahaziah do evil in the sight of the LORD?
options: Because the house of Ahab were his counsellors after his father's death
Because he wanted to please the inhabitants of Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: Because the house of Ahab were his counsellors after his father's death
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 22:4 states that Ahaziah did evil in the sight of the LORD like the house of Ahab because they were his counsellors after the death of his father.

questions.question: Whose death led to the house of Ahab being counsellors to Ahaziah to his destruction?
questions.correctAnswer: His father
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 22:4 says the house of Ahab were his counsellors after the death of his father to his destruction.

questions.question: True or False: Ahaziah was made king because the eldest sons were slain by men who came with the Arabians.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 22:1 explains that Ahaziah was made king because the band of men that came with the Arabians had slain all the eldest sons.

questions.question: True or False: Ahaziah's mother was Athaliah, the daughter of Omri.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 22:2 states that Ahaziah's mother was Athaliah, the daughter of Omri.

questions.question: True or False: The text states that Ahaziah reigned for ten years in Jerusalem.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 22:2 states that Ahaziah reigned only one year in Jerusalem, not ten years.

questions.question: True or False: The text says Ahaziah was counselled to do good by his mother.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 22:3 states that his mother was his counsellor to do wickedly, not good.

medium.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 22 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Chronicles Chapter 22 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Against whom did Ahaziah go to war alongside Jehoram the son of Ahab?
questions.correctAnswer: Hazael king of Syria
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 22:5 states that Ahaziah went with Jehoram the son of Ahab king of Israel to war against Hazael king of Syria at Ramothgilead.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 22:6 promise will happen if someone is wounded in battle as described in 2 Chronicles 22:5?
options: They will return to be healed
questions.correctAnswer: They will return to be healed
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 22:6 explains that after being wounded at Ramah fighting Hazael king of Syria (verse 5), he returned to be healed in Jezreel.

questions.question: Who went down to see Jehoram the son of Ahab because he was sick?
options: Azariah the son of Jehoram king of Judah
Ahaziah the son of Jehoram king of Judah
questions.correctAnswer: Azariah the son of Jehoram king of Judah
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 22:6 states that Azariah the son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to see Jehoram the son of Ahab at Jezreel because he was sick.

questions.question: How is the destruction of Ahaziah explained in relation to his visit to Jehoram?
options: It was ordained by God because he went to Joram
It was caused by the Syrians
It was due to injuries sustained in battle
It was because of his mother's counsel
questions.correctAnswer: It was ordained by God because he went to Joram
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 22:7 shows that the destruction of Ahaziah was of God by coming to Joram, as God had anointed Jehu to cut off the house of Ahab.

questions.question: What lesson can be learned about counsel and leadership from Ahaziah's actions in 2 Chronicles 22:5-7?
options: Following ungodly counsel can lead to destruction
Ignoring counsel is the best course
War is always the right decision
questions.correctAnswer: Following ungodly counsel can lead to destruction
questions.explanation: Ahaziah walked after the counsel of others (verse 5) and his destruction was ordained by God because of this (verse 7), teaching the importance of godly counsel.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 22:8 illustrate the consequences of being aligned with ungodly leadership?
options: Princes and ministers serving Ahaziah were slain by Jehu
questions.correctAnswer: Princes and ministers serving Ahaziah were slain by Jehu
questions.explanation: Verse 8 shows that Jehu slew the princes of Judah and ministers who served Ahaziah while executing judgment on the house of Ahab.

questions.question: What practical advice about alliances can be drawn from Ahaziah’s alliance with Jehoram king of Israel?
options: Aligning with ungodly leaders can bring harm
questions.correctAnswer: Aligning with ungodly leaders can bring harm
questions.explanation: Ahaziah’s alliance with Jehoram, who followed the ways of Ahab, led to his destruction (verses 5 and 7), demonstrating the risk of ungodly alliances.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 22:6 demonstrate the importance of caring for the sick and wounded?
options: Azariah went to see Jehoram because he was sick
Sick people were ignored in battle
questions.correctAnswer: Azariah went to see Jehoram because he was sick
questions.explanation: Verse 6 shows Azariah visiting Jehoram due to his sickness, highlighting the value of compassion and visiting those who are ill.

questions.question: What does the fate of Ahaziah’s family members in 2 Chronicles 22:8 teach about the consequences of leadership choices?
options: Family members serving ungodly leaders may suffer severe consequences
Family is always protected regardless of choices
God does not involve family in judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Family members serving ungodly leaders may suffer severe consequences
questions.explanation: In verse 8, Jehu kills the princes and sons of Ahaziah’s family who ministered to him, showing that following ungodly leadership can affect the whole family.

questions.question: Considering 2 Chronicles 22:5-8, what principle about divine judgment can be applied to Christian living?
options: God executes judgment on those following evil paths
questions.correctAnswer: God executes judgment on those following evil paths
questions.explanation: These verses show God’s judgment on Ahaziah and his associates due to their evil ways and alliances, teaching that God judges unrighteousness.

questions.question: What warning can Christians take from Ahaziah’s reliance on his mother’s counsel as implied in the broader chapter context?
options: Following ungodly counselors leads to destruction
Advice from parents is always correct
questions.correctAnswer: Following ungodly counselors leads to destruction
questions.explanation: Ahaziah followed his mother Athaliah's wicked counsel (2 Chronicles 22:3-4), which contributed to his downfall, warning believers to seek godly advice.

questions.question: How does the story of Ahaziah illustrate the importance of faithfulness to God's will rather than political or military alliances?
options: Ignoring God's will for alliances results in destruction
Political alliances always lead to success
God supports all kings regardless of faith
questions.correctAnswer: Ignoring God's will for alliances results in destruction
questions.explanation: Ahaziah’s alliance with Jehoram and involvement in war against God's anointed enemy led to his death (verses 5-7), showing that faithfulness to God is paramount.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 22:7 teach about God's sovereignty over the affairs of kings and nations?
options: God can ordain destruction of kings according to His purpose
God only blesses kings who make war
Nations are not subject to divine will
questions.correctAnswer: God can ordain destruction of kings according to His purpose
questions.explanation: Verse 7 states that Ahaziah’s destruction was of God because he came to Joram, showing God's sovereign control over kings' destinies.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Chronicles 22:8, Jehu spared all the princes of Judah who served Ahaziah while executing judgment on Ahab's house.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 8 states Jehu slew the princes of Judah and sons of Ahaziah’s brothers who ministered to Ahaziah, so he did not spare them.

questions.question: True or False: 2 Chronicles 22:6 shows Azariah went to see Jehoram at Jezreel because Jehoram was victorious and healthy after battle.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The verse clearly says Azariah went to see Jehoram because he was sick, not because he was healthy or victorious.

hard.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 22 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Chronicles Chapter 22.

questions.question: Who was hidden in Samaria before being caught and brought to Jehu according to 2 Chronicles 22:9?
questions.correctAnswer: Ahaziah
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 22:9 states that Ahaziah was hid in Samaria and then caught and brought to Jehu.

questions.question: Why was Ahaziah buried despite being slain by Jehu's men?
options: Because he sought the LORD with all his heart
Because he was the son of Jehoshaphat
Because he was the king of Judah
questions.correctAnswer: Because he was the son of Jehoshaphat
questions.explanation: In 2 Chronicles 22:9, they buried Ahaziah because he was the son of Jehoshaphat, who sought the LORD with all his heart.

questions.question: What was Athaliah's reaction upon seeing that her son Ahaziah was dead?
options: She destroyed all the royal seed of Judah
questions.correctAnswer: She destroyed all the royal seed of Judah
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 22:10 says that Athaliah arose and destroyed all the seed royal of the house of Judah after Ahaziah's death.

questions.question: Who hid Joash, the son of Ahaziah, to protect him from Athaliah?
questions.correctAnswer: Jehoshabeath
questions.explanation: According to 2 Chronicles 22:11, Jehoshabeath, the daughter of the king, hid Joash from Athaliah to protect him.

questions.question: For how many years was Joash hidden in the house of God while Athaliah reigned?
questions.correctAnswer: Six years
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 22:12 explains that Joash was hidden in the house of God for six years during Athaliah's reign.

questions.question: What relation was Jehoshabeath to Ahaziah and Jehoram?
options: Sister of Ahaziah and daughter of Jehoram
Daughter of Ahaziah and sister of Jehoram
Mother of Ahaziah and wife of Jehoram
Aunt of Ahaziah and mother of Jehoram
questions.correctAnswer: Sister of Ahaziah and daughter of Jehoram
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 22:11 states Jehoshabeath was the daughter of king Jehoram and sister of Ahaziah.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'natsar' (נָצַר) in 2 Chronicles 22:11 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: To guard or keep
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'natsar' in 2 Chronicles 22:11 means 'to guard or keep,' fitting the context of hiding Joash for protection.

questions.question: Which literary device best describes the narrative of Joash being hidden while Athaliah reigns?
questions.correctAnswer: Typology
questions.explanation: The hidden Joash story is a typology foreshadowing later messianic salvation themes, shown in 2 Chronicles 22:12.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of a rightful heir hidden to preserve the lineage, as in 2 Chronicles 22:11-12?
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 2:13-15
questions.explanation: Matthew 2:13-15 recounts Jesus being hidden in Egypt to protect Him from Herod, paralleling Joash’s protection in 2 Chronicles 22:11-12.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage fulfills the judgment upon Athaliah and the house of Ahab as described in 2 Chronicles 22:7-8?
questions.correctAnswer: 2 Kings 9:1-37
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 9:1-37 describes Jehu’s anointing and judgment on Ahab’s house, directly paralleling 2 Chronicles 22:7-8.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes the hiding of Joash in 2 Chronicles 22?
questions.correctAnswer: Athaliah destroys the royal seed
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 22:10 describes Athaliah destroying the royal seed before Jehoshabeath hides Joash in verse 11.

questions.question: The term 'seed royal' in 2 Chronicles 22:10 exemplifies which literary device?
questions.correctAnswer: Metonymy
questions.explanation: 'Seed royal' is metonymy using 'seed' to represent the royal descendants, as seen in 2 Chronicles 22:10.

questions.question: Which historical-cultural context explains Athaliah’s act of destroying the royal seed in 2 Chronicles 22:10?
options: To eliminate rivals and secure power
questions.correctAnswer: To eliminate rivals and secure power
questions.explanation: Athaliah’s destruction of the royal seed was a political move to eliminate rivals and secure her reign, per 2 Chronicles 22:10.

questions.question: The phrase 'he sought Ahaziah' in 2 Chronicles 22:9 is best understood as?
options: Jehu’s men searched for Ahaziah to kill him
Ahaziah hid himself from the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Jehu’s men searched for Ahaziah to kill him
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 22:9 explains that Jehu’s men sought Ahaziah to capture and kill him.

questions.question: True or False: Jehoshabeath was the wife of Jehoiada the priest and hid Joash from Athaliah.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 22:11 states Jehoshabeath was the wife of Jehoiada and hid Joash from Athaliah.

theological.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 22 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Chronicles Chapter 22 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Chronicles 22:3 teach about human sin?
options: Sin often propagates through ungodly counsel and influence
Sin is primarily a result of external circumstances beyond one’s control
Sin is only punished if it is committed publicly
Sin cannot be avoided if one is born into a sinful lineage
questions.correctAnswer: Sin often propagates through ungodly counsel and influence
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 22:3 states that Ahaziah walked in the ways of the house of Ahab because his mother was his counsellor to do wickedly, demonstrating how sinful influence leads to further sin.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine judgment does 2 Chronicles 22:7 teach?
options: God sovereignly ordains instruments of judgment to fulfill His purposes
God’s judgment is arbitrary and based on human whim
Judgment always comes immediately upon sin
God’s judgment is limited to the nation of Israel alone
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly ordains instruments of judgment to fulfill His purposes
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 22:7 explains that Ahaziah's destruction was by God through Jehu, whom the LORD had anointed to cut off the house of Ahab, showing divine sovereignty in executing judgment.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning the influence of the covenant family does 2 Chronicles 22:9 teach?
options: The legacy of a godly ancestor can affect how one is treated even after death
Covenantal blessings are guaranteed regardless of personal faithfulness
Family lineage ensures protection from divine judgment
God’s promises to a family are unconditional and eternal
questions.correctAnswer: The legacy of a godly ancestor can affect how one is treated even after death
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 22:9 shows that Ahaziah was buried because he was the son of Jehoshaphat who sought the LORD with all his heart, indicating the impact of a godly legacy.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 22:10 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Justice
questions.explanation: Verse 10 describes Athaliah destroying the royal seed, illustrating God's justice as He allows consequences for evil actions.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 22:12 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Providence
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 22:12 shows God’s providence in preserving Joash hidden in the house of God during Athaliah’s reign.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 22:5 connect to the broader biblical theme of divine retribution?
options: It exemplifies the consequences of unfaithfulness to God through military defeat
It shows that God always protects His people from physical harm
It teaches that political alliances guarantee divine favor
It suggests that human warfare is independent of divine will
questions.correctAnswer: It exemplifies the consequences of unfaithfulness to God through military defeat
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 22:5 recounts Jehoram and Ahaziah’s defeat by Hazael, demonstrating God’s retribution for unfaithfulness as seen throughout Scripture.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 22:11 prepare for the Messianic hope in redemptive history?
options: By showing God’s preservation of the Davidic line through Joash
By emphasizing the failure of all royal lines to survive
By depicting the end of covenant promises
By illustrating the futility of human resistance to evil
questions.correctAnswer: By showing God’s preservation of the Davidic line through Joash
questions.explanation: Verse 11 narrates Jehoshabeath hiding Joash, preserving the royal line from which the Messiah would come, a key theme in biblical redemption.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 3 and 4 teach about human sin and divine judgment?
options: Sinful counsel leads to evil deeds which invoke God’s righteous judgment
Human sin is excusable under bad guidance
Divine judgment is unrelated to human actions
Sin can be inherited and is irreversible
questions.correctAnswer: Sinful counsel leads to evil deeds which invoke God’s righteous judgment
questions.explanation: Verses 3 and 4 show Ahaziah’s evil ways under his mother’s counsel and the resulting divine displeasure, illustrating the link between sin and judgment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 7 and 8 teach about God’s sovereignty in judgment and human agency?
options: God sovereignly ordains human agents to execute His judgment
Divine judgment is random and unpredictable
Humans act independently of God’s will
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly ordains human agents to execute His judgment
questions.explanation: Verses 7 and 8 show Jehu as God’s anointed agent executing judgment, affirming divine sovereignty working through human agency.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 9 and 10 teach about divine justice and mercy in royal succession?
options: God’s justice punishes evil but His mercy preserves a remnant
God’s mercy guarantees all kings a peaceful reign
Justice and mercy are irrelevant in royal politics
Mercy is shown by allowing all royal descendants to reign
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice punishes evil but His mercy preserves a remnant
questions.explanation: Verse 9 mentions Ahaziah’s burial due to his godly father, while verse 10 shows Athaliah’s destruction of the royal line, illustrating justice and mercy in succession.

questions.question: Sceptics claim 2 Chronicles 22:10-12 condones violence and political intrigue. What does this passage actually teach?
options: It teaches God’s providential preservation of His covenant despite human evil
It endorses violent overthrow as God’s primary method
It shows that God is indifferent to royal bloodlines
It suggests that human schemes dictate God’s plan
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches God’s providential preservation of His covenant despite human evil
questions.explanation: Verses 10-12 show Athaliah’s destruction but also God’s providence in hiding Joash, affirming divine preservation over human evil.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Chronicles 22:1 teach about divine permissiveness and human responsibility?
options: God permits certain events but humans remain responsible for evil acts
God directly causes every evil action
Humans have no responsibility for events ordained by God
God is uninvolved in earthly affairs
questions.correctAnswer: God permits certain events but humans remain responsible for evil acts
questions.explanation: Verse 1 shows men coming with Arabians killing the eldest sons, indicating God's permissiveness, but human agents carried out the evil deed.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 22:6 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Mercy
questions.explanation: The verse describes Jehoram wounded but alive, and his brother Azariah visiting him, showing God’s mercy in prolonging life amid judgment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 11 and 12 teach about sanctification and divine protection?
options: Sanctification includes God’s protection of His chosen remnant
Sanctification is purely individual and unrelated to divine intervention
Divine protection is guaranteed to all without exception
The sanctuary was irrelevant to God’s saving purposes
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification includes God’s protection of His chosen remnant
questions.explanation: Verses 11-12 show Jehoshabeath hiding Joash in the house of God, highlighting God’s protection as part of sanctification.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 22:2 contribute to the biblical doctrine of covenant and apostasy?
options: It illustrates how covenantal blessing can be undermined by apostasy within the royal family
It shows covenant blessings are unconditional
It denies any correlation between lineage and faithfulness
It teaches that apostasy is not possible for kings
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates how covenantal blessing can be undermined by apostasy within the royal family
questions.explanation: Verse 2 identifies Athaliah, daughter of Omri, as Ahaziah’s mother, correlating to apostasy influencing covenant failure.
